AboutHackathonAgendaSpeakersVenueSponsorsVolunteersFAQContactRegister for free

October 13, 2026 · AWS Builder Loft

← AWS Community Day 2026

Agentic AI Hackathon

Participant Guide

Build an agent that does real work on AWS.

Two weeks. One track. Eight teams demo live on stage at AWS Community Day in front of 200+ builders. Up to $3,200 in AWS credits on the line.

Build window: Tuesday, September 29 to Tuesday, October 13, 2026
Submissions due: Sunday, October 11, 11:59 PM PT
Finals: AWS Community Day, AI Edition, October 13, 2026, AWS Builder Loft, 525 Market St, Floor 2, San Francisco, CA 94105
Teams and announcements: the hackathon Slack channel. The invite and channel links are in your kickoff email.
Questions: Ask in the Slack channel so everyone gets the answer, or use Contact the Host on the Luma page for anything private. Replies within 24 hours.
The challenge: Hand it off

Build an agent that takes over a task a specific person does by hand every week, and produces something that person would accept without redoing it.

Three requirements, and judges will check all three:

Name the person. A real role, not a persona: a clinic scheduler, an on-call SRE, a landlord with twelve units. Your writeup says who they are and what the task costs them today.
Call at least one tool you didn't build. An AWS service via tool use, a public API, or an MCP server. The agent has to act, not just talk.
Show the failure path. Your demo video shows what happens when that tool fails, returns garbage, or disagrees with the model. Happy path only is a demo, not an agent.

Everything else is open: domain, model, framework, number of agents.

What this is not: a chatbot with a nice UI, a RAG app that answers questions about documents, or a pipeline where a human still does the last step.

No project yet? Eight starter ideas that already meet all three requirements are posted in the Slack channel. Pick one, adapt it, or bring your own, and choose a lead by end of day Friday, October 2.

Two weeks is enough for a working prototype, not a finished product. Judges know that. Scope accordingly.

Your team
Registration closed on September 28 and teams are formed. Team assignments are posted in the hackathon Slack channel.
Teams are capped at 4. Solo registrants are matched by project theme, and each team has a lead: the person who brought the idea.
Find your team, email your teammates, and create a channel named #hack-<your team>, for example #hack-s07. If you can't reach someone by Friday, October 2, DM the hackathon lead and you will be reassigned.
You must be registered for AWS Community Day. Finalists present in person, and you can't be called on stage without it.
Organizers, judges, and their immediate work teammates can't win prizes.
Not registered for Community Day yet? Register here, it is free.
Rules
All hackathon work starts on or after September 29, when the kickoff email went out. Open-source libraries and frameworks are fine. Renaming an existing project is not.
Your project must meet all three challenge requirements above.
Use at least two AWS services, and at least one must be an AI service: Bedrock, AgentCore, Strands, SageMaker, Transcribe, Rekognition, and similar all count.
Your code must be in a public GitHub repo. Private repos, invite-only links, and zip files will not be accepted. The repo must be public at the time you submit and stay public through October 13. License it MIT or Apache 2.0.
No production customer data, PHI, or PII. Use synthetic or public datasets.
You own your IP. We just want to see it.
Be kind. The event code of conduct applies to every channel and the day itself.
Timeline
Date	What happensMon Sep 28	Registration closed.
Tue Sep 29	Hackathon starts. Kickoff email goes out with team assignments, the challenge and the rules. Build begins.
Fri Oct 2	Teams without a project pick one and choose a lead. Teammates who can't be reached get reassigned.
Mon Oct 5	Submission form and writeup template posted in the Slack channel.
Sep 29 to Oct 11	Build. Questions go in the hackathon Slack channel.
Sun Oct 11, 11:59 PM PT	Submissions due. No extensions.
Mon Oct 12 by 6 PM PT	Finalists notified by email.
Tue Oct 13	Community Day. Finalists check in at the hackathon room, dry-run on the main stage over lunch, demo live at 4:15 PM after the closing remarks. Winners announced right after the last demo.
How to submit

By Sunday, October 11, 11:59 PM PT, submit via the submission form. The four items below won't change, so build toward them now.

Public GitHub repo (MIT or Apache 2.0) with a README that runs. We open the link logged out; if it 404s, it doesn't count.
3-minute demo video, YouTube unlisted or Loom. Include the failure path. This is also your backup if the live demo fails, so make it good.
One-page writeup using the template: who the person is, what the task costs them today, an architecture diagram, AWS services used, and what you'd build next.
Team roster with names and emails. This is how credits get issued, so get it right. No roster changes after the deadline.

The writeup template is posted in the Slack channel by Monday, October 5.

How you'll be judged

Every criterion is scored 1 to 5 by each judge.

Technical depth

30%

A 5 looks like: Real agentic behavior (planning, tool use, memory), sound AWS architecture, more than a prompt wrapper

Real-world usefulness

25%

A 5 looks like: Solves a problem a real user has, clear target user, plausible path to adoption

Responsible AI

20%

A 5 looks like: Guardrails, handles failure and hallucination, considers privacy and misuse, cites data sources

Demo and communication

15%

A 5 looks like: Works live, tells a clear story, honest about limitations

Completeness and polish

10%

A 5 looks like: Runs from the README, has tests or evals, clean repo

Round 1 (Oct 12): Judges score every submission asynchronously from your video, repo, and writeup. The top 8 become finalists.

Round 2 (Oct 13): Finalists demo live and are re-scored. You get 5 minutes, hard stop, with a visible timer. Judges may ask a quick question or two in the 1-minute changeover. Final score is 40% Round 1 and 60% live demo.

Judges decide right after the eighth demo and the winners are announced on stage before the room empties, around 5:00 PM.

Prizes
Winning team: $2,000 in AWS credits ($500 per member, up to 4 members)
Runner-up team: $1,200 in AWS credits ($300 per member, up to 4 members)

All 8 finalists get their demo recorded and featured on the AWS Community Bay Area YouTube channel, plus a shout-out from the organizers on LinkedIn.

Credits are AWS promotional credits applied to your own AWS account, issued within about two weeks after the event. Make sure every team member has an AWS account in their own name. Promotional credits typically have an expiry date and some service restrictions; we'll share the exact terms when codes are issued.

Finalist day-of checklist (Oct 13)
Arrive when doors open at 9:30 AM and check in at the hackathon room (the Track B room, yours until 2:00 PM).
Do the mandatory dry run with a volunteer on the main stage during lunch, 1:00 to 2:00 PM. Every team, no exceptions.
Bring your own laptop, charger, and any adapters. We'll have HDMI and USB-C at the stage.
Have your backup video open in a tab.
Practice the 5-minute version. Then practice the 4-minute version.
Tips from the organizers
Pick the demo moment first, then build backward from it.
A narrow agent that reliably does one thing beats a broad agent that sometimes does five.
Show the failure handling. Judges love seeing what happens when the tool call errors out.
Ask early. Nobody has ever regretted posting a question in the channel on October 3 instead of discovering the problem on October 11.

See you on stage October 13.

About Event

​A 10-hour hackathon where you go from a plain-English spec to firmware running on a real dev board, or to a computer vision model doing real-time inference on a GPU, using CraftifAI's AI agents for hardware engineers.

​📅 Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026 · 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM PT
📍 San Francisco, CA
👤 Individual participation, no teams
🛠 Dev boards and sensors provided, cloud GPUs available

​Why we're running this

​AI coding agents changed how software gets shipped, but embedded development has barely moved. Ask a general-purpose model for an STM32 peripheral driver and you often get code that compiles cleanly, then fails on the bench because the model guessed the clock tree configuration or the pin mux. Firmware and on-device AI depend on hardware context that chat-based tools never see.

​CraftifAI builds agents that work with that context. FirmGen writes, compiles, debugs and flashes firmware for ESP32 and STM32 MCUs. PipeGen turns Python CV code and ONNX models into optimized, production-ready NVIDIA DeepStream apps, benchmarked and containerized. This hackathon is your chance to put both to the test on real hardware, in a single day.

The Universal Celebration Hackathon is a celebration of creativity, entrepreneurship, and the next generation of AI-powered companies. Bring your ideas, experiment with new possibilities, and turn your vision into something real.
This hackathon is about more than building a prototype. It’s about imagining what a company looks like when AI agents can work together as a team.

Build a company run by a team of AI agents.
Your challenge is to create an AI-native business or startup where multiple specialized agents work together to build, operate, and grow the company.

You might have a CEO agent defining strategy, a product agent building the product, engineering agents writing code, marketing agents finding customers, sales agents closing deals, finance agents managing the business, and operations or customer-support agents keeping everything running.

​Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time. 

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!
